newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares firm, seen powering into new year.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares firm, seen powering into new year.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares opened the week firmer with brokers saying they expected them to power ahead into the new year on continuing strong investor sentiment.

The key 57-share industrial index surged 33.48 points to close at a new all time high of 8,781.48, boosted mainly by glass firm PG Industries' 50-cent rise to 560 and sugar refinery ZSR's 35-cent jump to 1,450.
"The buyers are still around and sentiment is strong. I think industrials will continue strong into the new year," one broker said.
"There's a lot of money on the money market and rates are low and together with current rains, this is helping the rise on the stock market," he added.

Among Monday's winners, cement producer Circle rose 35 cents to 850, pharmaceutical group Caps gained 30 cents to 350 clothing retailer Truworths added 20 cents to 990 while rubber products firm Acacia, engineering group Gulliver and local conglomerate TA Holdings all put on 10 cents to 350, 240 and 170 respectively.
Against the trend, clothing and furniture retailer Tedco shed 20 cents to 980 and construction company Mash lost 10 cents to 290.
Minings were quiet with Wankie Colliery gaining 10 cents to 560 but gold producer Ashanti fell 1,000 cents to 10,000 and Falgold eased five cents to 105.
The seven-counter mining index ended a marginal 1.5 points down at 1,064.84.
